messages:
maria: @here quick follow-up from the Dedicated GPU pool RFC — I sketched a "safety layers" contract between the allocator and the scale controller. want quick sanity checks before i turn it into a formal proposal.

chris: curious, what does "safety layers" mean here? is this about headroom vs cost or more like escape hatches when capacity is low?

maria: both. idea is 3 layers: 1) admission guard (reject if no headroom), 2) soft headroom (admit but mark for prewarm), 3) emergency fallback (route to shared/hosted with throttles). separates concerns so allocator only enforces invariants and scaler handles remedial actions.

alex: that separation sounds sane. need to be explicit about semantics: does "admission guard" have to be binary? can we expose a tunable threshold per-tenant?

maria: yes per-tenant threshold is required. defaults from infra but customers can set conservative budgets. also tracks "credit" buckets so bursty tenants can occasionally exceed but get charged/penalized.

rita: how do we represent these contracts in the operator API? i worry about adding too many fields to pool CRDs.

maria: proposal: keep operator surface small, expose a single "safety_profile" enum + a freeform "custom_constraints" map for advanced tenants. allocator interprets profile into numeric invariants. example: 
```yaml
poolSafetyProfile: balanced  # {conservative, balanced, aggressive}
custom_constraints:
  min_headroom_pct: 10
  max_burst_tokens: 500
```

chris: ok. what about prewarm semantics? do we let scaler prewarm on tenant hints or only on admission spikes? prewarming GPUs is expensive.

maria: prefer hint-driven prewarm. ingress layer emits short-lived "request hints" with expected QPS and model size; scaler aggregates and opens prewarm reservations if aggregated headroom < threshold for N minutes.

alex: we need an accounting model for cost and billing. if tenant uses prewarm and never sends traffic, who pays?

rita: tie prewarm tokens to tenant credits: allocation consumes soft-reservation credits; unused credits expire and are reported. billing layer converts credits to dollars.

chris: eviction policy: if allocator crams nodes, how do we pick which soft-reserved containers to evict? priority + recency?

maria: evict in this order: 1) prewarm reservations (lowest priority), 2) soft-reserved burst tasks, 3) best-effort shared tasks. do not evict hard-reserved or on-demand live requests. add grace TTL to let clients retry.

alex: fallback path: route to hosted inference. how transparent should that be to apps? automatic or explicit opt-in?

maria: automatic with a tenant-level opt-out. default: failover enabled for higher reliability. SDK surfaces a header so apps can detect fallback and optionally degrade features.

deploy-bot: deploy status: new allocator-metrics exporter to staging at 1748545120 :rocket:

rita: one more thing — observability. we need token-level traces for admission decisions + cost tags. without that, debugging will be a nightmare.

maria: agreed. plan to add an "admission_reason" tag and numeric vectors: headroom_left_pct, credits_remaining, prewarm_active. these are emitted per-request and aggregated.

chris: sounds comprehensive. edge-case: network partition between allocator and scaler. do we default to safe (reject) or permissive (allow)?

maria: default to safe: reject new admissions but keep serving existing sessions. with a heartbeat TTL so we can fail-open only if operator flips an override switch.

alex: lgtm with comments. can you put the sketch into a short RFC doc and link the open questions at top? happy to review.

maria: will do. i'll add decision table and sample operator CRD patches. thanks all :thumbsup:
